newsitem.title: FRANCE: Soc Gen calls for breakup of Cr Lyonnais.
newsitem.headline: Soc Gen calls for breakup of Cr Lyonnais.

text.p: Societe Generale Chairman Marc Vienot reiterated his call for the breakup and liquidation of state-owned Credit Lyonnais in a newspaper interview on Monday.

"With two successive (rescue) plans in 1994 and 1995, Lyonnais has received assistance -- described by the European Commission as colossal -- that will be financed by taxpayers to the year 2014," he told the financial daily La Tribune.
He said the assistance was estimated at at least 120 billion francs, not including the loss of 60 billion of the bank's equity prior to its economic difficulties.
The French government is expected later this month to present its latest bailout package for the troubled bank.
Societe Generale is preparing to lodge a second protest with the Commission over the plan. Vienot said Credit Lyonnais had not fulfilled conditions for approval of previous plans.

"Societe Generale feels the Commission should compensate the damages caused to its (Credit Lyonnais') competitors by imposing the sale of all its foreign activities -- including those in the United States and Southeast Asia, which would be the easiest to sell for profit, and also activities in France such as property management, consumer credit or life insurance," he said.
"This sale by pieces would generate resources to reduce the taxpayer's burden and would support the local banking network in full or in part," he said.
Vienot has previously said it would be "stunning if our fellow bank kept its profitable assets to compete with us and made the tax payer foot the bill for the sale of its unprofitable assets."
